1	# The seven-tier access ladder
2	
3	Work down it in order. **Stop at the highest rung that works, and tell the
4	customer what they gave up by not being one rung higher.** Never skip a
5	rung without saying why — "we built a custom API wrapper" is the wrong
6	answer when a vendor MCP existed and nobody looked.
7	
8	| Tier | Path | Freshness | Build cost | Who maintains it | The catch |
9	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
10	| 1 | Vendor-native / hosted MCP already exists | Real-time | None — setup only | The vendor | You inherit the vendor's scope exactly, including its limits |
11	| 2 | Community or third-party MCP | Real-time | Low — evaluate and wire | Nobody, unless you fork it | You own it the moment it breaks |
12	| 3 | Documented API → scoped custom MCP wrapper | Real-time | Medium | You | API access may be a paid license tier; rate limits; vendor deprecation |
13	| 4 | Read-only database view or replica | Near-real-time | Medium | You and the customer's DBA | Schema changes break it silently; may void vendor support |
14	| 5 | Zapier / iPaaS bridge | Minutes (polled) | Low | Zapier and you | Limited to exposed triggers/actions; per-task cost; another vendor in the data path |
15	| 6 | Screen-level automation (RPA) | Varies | High | You, constantly | Fragile, and often prohibited by vendor terms |
16	| 7 | Scheduled export contract | Export cadence | Low | Customer's IT | Not real-time; silently stops running |
17	
18	**One deliberate crossover:** for bulk or historical data, skip Tiers 5 and
19	6 and go straight to Tier 7. Pulling three months of production history
20	through Zapier is slow, expensive and pointless when a nightly CSV does it
21	properly. **Use Tier 5 for events** — "a work order was created," "a
22	quality hold was raised" — **Tier 7 for volume.**
23	
24	---
25	
26	## What the skill delivers, and what a person still does
27	
28	A Claude skill produces artifacts. It does not stand up and host
29	infrastructure — that's the boundary that decides what "as far as it can
30	go" means at every rung.
31	
32	| Tier | What the skill produces | What a person does |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| 1 — Vendor MCP | Research finding, plan-tier check, step-by-step setup instructions, scope recommendation, a test call once connected | The customer's admin generates credentials and enables the connector |
35	| 2 — Community MCP | Evaluation (currency, maintainer, requested scope, security review), a recommendation, setup instructions | The customer or engineer installs it |
36	| 3 — API wrapper | The API assessment, the scoped surface design, the generated wrapper code, the field mapping, deployment instructions | An engineer reviews, deploys and hosts it |
37	| 4 — DB view | The view definition or SQL, the field mapping, the access request to hand the DBA | The customer's DBA creates the view and grants read access |
38	| 5 — Zapier bridge | The Zap specification — trigger, filter, action, field mapping, destination — plus the cost estimate at their volume | The customer builds it in Zapier's UI |
39	| 6 — RPA | A recommendation against it, with the specific reasons | Nothing, preferably |
40	| 7 — Export contract | The complete export specification — fields, types, format, cadence, naming, landing path | The customer's IT builds the scheduled export |
41	
42	Read down the right-hand column and the pattern holds throughout: **the
43	skill removes the thinking, the research and the writing; a person
44	performs the privileged action.** That's not a limitation — it's the same
45	approval boundary the rest of the plugin runs on, and it's what makes a
46	connector skill safe to ship.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Tier 1 — A vendor-native or hosted MCP already exists
51	
52	**The most common good outcome, and the one most likely to be missed.**
53	Several manufacturing vendors have shipped MCP servers quietly, without
54	announcing them anywhere the customer would see. The job here is not to
55	build anything — it's to recognize the situation and walk the customer's
56	admin through turning it on.
57

59	
60	- Where in the vendor's admin console to generate credentials, named

62	- What scope to request — read-only unless a write is genuinely needed
63	- Whether the customer's plan tier includes it, and what to do if it
64	  doesn't

67	- A test call that proves it works, with real records shown back

1	# Handling credentials, and saying how it will break
2	
3	---
4	
5	## Credentials
6	
7	**Narrowest scope that does the job.** Read-only unless a write is
8	genuinely required and has been approved — not "might be useful later,"
9	approved for a stated, current need.
10	
11	**A dedicated integration user, never someone's personal login.** Access
12	tied to a person breaks the day they change roles or leave, usually at the
13	worst possible moment, and it can't be revoked without locking that person
14	out of everything else they use the same login for.
15	
16	**Tokens and OAuth only. Never a password.** A password is a standing
17	secret with no expiry and no scope; a token can be scoped, rotated, and
18	revoked without touching anything else the account can do.
19	
20	**Say plainly what the connector will be able to reach before it's
21	created.** Not after — the customer's admin is granting access based on
22	what they're told, and finding out afterward that the scope was broader
23	than expected is how a plant stops trusting the next connector request.
24	
25	**Never accept a credential in conversation.** Not pasted, not typed, not
26	read back to confirm it was copied correctly. If someone pastes one
27	anyway, say plainly that it should be rotated — a credential that has
28	touched a chat transcript is not clean again just because nobody used it.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Registering what was built
33	
34	Once a connector is working, record — concretely, not as a general
35	capability claim:
36	
37	- **What it reaches.** The specific entities and fields, not "NetSuite
38	  data."
39	- **What it cannot do.** The boundary is as important as the capability;
40	  a downstream skill needs to know what to ask for elsewhere.
41	- **How it refreshes.** Real-time, polled at an interval, or on an export
42	  cadence — and what that means for anything time-sensitive that reads it.
43	- **Which skills it now unblocks.** Named specifically, so the person who
44	  requested it can see the actual payoff.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Say how it will break, while the customer is still listening
49	
50	**A connector that fails silently is worse than no connector.** No
51	connector produces an obvious gap; a silently failing one produces
52	confident, wrong output that looks exactly like a working connection.
53	
54	State the specific failure mode for the tier that was built, before
55	handing it over:
56	
57	| Tier | How it fails |
58	|---|---|
59	| 1, 2, 3 | Token expiry — name the renewal path. Vendor API version changes arrive with no warning; the surface needs re-testing when they do |
60	| 3 | Rate limits, hit under real load rather than in testing |
61	| 4 | Schema drift — a vendor upgrade changes the underlying table with no error, and the view returns the wrong thing or nothing |
62	| 5 | Task limits on the plan tier, and per-task cost that scales with volume nobody budgeted for |
63	| 7 | An export that stops landing, silently, with no error anywhere — this is exactly why `data-consolidate`'s freshness check exists |
64	
65	**Name who fixes it, too.** A failure mode with no owner is a failure mode
66	nobody responds to until a downstream skill reports something wrong and
67	someone traces it back here.

2	
3	**Emitted by** `data-consolidate`
4	**Consumed by** every data-dependent skill — as the default source, not the
5	only one; see *What this dataset is authoritative for* below — and it is the
6	mapping target for `custom-connector`
7	**Chain** 1, RFQ to quote (step 2) and 3, Morning plant pulse (step 1)
8	**Contract version** 6
9	
10	Rules that govern every contract are in [README.md](README.md).
11	
12	This file names the tabs
13	and columns so a consumer and a producer cannot invent two different shapes.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Form
18	
19	One queryable working file. **Excel workbook, one tab per entity, is the v1
20	format. The writer is swappable.** The shape below is the contract.
21	
22	If `data-consolidate` pulled a record type, that type has a tab. A pulled input
23	with no tab is how inventory went missing the first time this file was written.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Entity tabs
28	
29	The join hangs off five anchors: part, production work order,
30	sales order, lot, asset. Every other input is an entity too. It gets its
31	own tab. It is not folded onto an anchor.
32	
33	### The five anchors
34	
35	| Tab | Grain | Key | Fields |
36	|---|---|---|---|
37	| `parts` | One row per part | Part number | Description, standard cost, UOM |
38	| `production_work_orders` | One row per production work order | Production work order number | Part, qty ordered, due date, status, and from version 5 the sales order it is built for (`sales_order` / `sales_order_verbatim`, null where the source holds no link). From version 6, closed-job cost where the ERP holds it: `actual_material_cost`, `actual_labor_cost`, `actual_burden_cost`, `actual_subcontract_cost` (each with `currency`), `qty_completed`, `closed_date`, `revision`, all nullable |
39	| `sales_orders` | One row per sales order line | Sales order number | Customer, part, qty, promised date, price |
40	| `lots` | One row per lot or batch | Lot number | The identity stamped on a quantity of material |
41	| `assets` | One row per machine | Asset ID | Location |
42	
43	### The other inputs
44	
45	| Tab | Grain | Joins on | Fields |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| `inventory` | One row per part per location | Part | On-hand qty, location |
48	| `purchase_orders` | One row per PO line | Part, supplier ID | Supplier, part, qty, cost, delivery date |
49	| `production_output` | One row per work order per shift per production day | Production work order, part | Qty good, qty scrap, shift, production day. **Two rows at the same grain are a duplicate key (class 8); the same work order on another shift is not** |
50	| `downtime_events` | One row per stoppage | Asset | Start, end, reason code |
51	| `inspection_results` | One row per measurement | Lot or production work order | Measurement vs spec |
52	| `maintenance_work_orders` | One row per maintenance ticket | Asset | Maintenance work order, dates, close-out notes |
53	| `plan` | One row per part per date | Part | Planned qty, date |
54	| `ncrs` | One row per NCR | Production work order, part, lot | NCR ID, found at, description verbatim, status, customer. |
55	
56	`inventory` is on-hand **by part and location**. A single on-hand total on
57	`parts` is not this tab. Containment needs the location.
58	
59	Supplier is a join key, not an anchor. It lives on `purchase_orders`.
60	
61	**`ncrs` is where an NCR export lands, and the NCR-to-work-order check runs on
62	it**: the NCR's part against the part the ERP holds for the work order it

"""Read-only schema inspection of the CMMS SQLite file. Opens with mode=ro + query_only."""
import sqlite3, sys, pathlib

p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{p.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
con.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON")
for t, n, sql in con.execute("select type,name,sql from sqlite_master order by type,name").fetchall():
    print(f"--- {t} {n}\n{sql}")
    if t in ("table", "view"):
        print("rows:", con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{n}"').fetchone()[0])
print("--- meta")
for r in con.execute("select * from meta"):
    print(r)
for t in ("assets", "work_orders", "v_open_work_orders"):
    print(f"--- sample {t}")
    cur = con.execute(f'select * from "{t}" limit 4')
    print([d[0] for d in cur.description])
    for r in cur:
        print(r)

"""
CMMS SQLite connector (Tier 4: read-only database access) - SYNTHETIC test target.

Reads assets and maintenance work orders from the CMMS SQLite file and maps them
onto the consolidated dataset schema (contract v6): tabs `assets` and
`maintenance_work_orders`.

Read-only is enforced three ways:
  1. the file is opened with the SQLite URI flag mode=ro (the OS handle is read-only),
  2. PRAGMA query_only=ON on the connection,
  3. SHA-256 of the file is taken before and after the run and must be identical.

No credentials are used: the target is a local file with no authentication.

Usage:
  python -I cmms_sqlite_connector.py <path-to-sqlite> <output-folder>
"""
import csv
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import sqlite3
import sys

SOURCE_SYSTEM = "cmms"
TODAY = dt.date(2026, 11, 15)  # session date; used for the future_timestamp check

# Schema fingerprint the mapping was built against. Any drift stops the run
# loudly instead of returning wrong or empty data (the Tier 4 failure mode).
EXPECTED_SCHEMA = {
    "assets": ["asset_id", "description", "site"],
    "work_orders": ["wo", "asset_id", "opened", "closed", "wo_type", "downtime_min", "note"],
}

COMMON = ["site", "source_system", "source_ref", "as_of", "join_status",
          "mismatch_class", "contradicted_by", "integrity_flags"]
ASSET_COLS = COMMON + ["asset_id", "asset_id_verbatim", "location"]
MWO_COLS = COMMON + ["maintenance_wo", "asset_id", "asset_id_verbatim",
                     "opened_date", "closed_date", "close_out_notes"]


def sha256(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def norm_key(v):
    """Ladder rungs 1-2 only (trim, upper-case). Nothing more aggressive is applied."""
    return None if v is None else v.strip().upper()


def parse_date(v):
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(v) if v else None
    except ValueError:
        return "unparseable"


def main(db_path, out_dir):
    db = pathlib.Path(db_path).resolve()
    out = pathlib.Path(out_dir).resolve()
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    hash_before = sha256(db)

    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    con.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON")
    query_only = con.execute("PRAGMA query_only").fetchone()[0]

    # --- schema drift check -------------------------------------------------
    drift = {}
    for table, cols in EXPECTED_SCHEMA.items():
        actual = [r[1] for r in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{table}")')]
        if actual != cols:
            drift[table] = {"expected": cols, "actual": actual}
    if drift:
        raise SystemExit(f"SCHEMA DRIFT - mapping not applied: {json.dumps(drift)}")

    # --- pull (explicit column lists, never SELECT *) ------------------------
    assets_raw = con.execute(
        "SELECT rowid, asset_id, description, site FROM assets ORDER BY asset_id").fetchall()
    wos_raw = con.execute(
        "SELECT rowid, wo, asset_id, opened, closed, wo_type, downtime_min, note "
        "FROM work_orders ORDER BY opened, wo").fetchall()

    # independent counts from the source itself (same file - see test notes)
    n_assets_src = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM assets").fetchone()[0]
    n_wo_src = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM work_orders").fetchone()[0]
    n_open_view = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM v_open_work_orders").fetchone()[0]
    n_open_tbl = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM work_orders WHERE closed IS NULL").fetchone()[0]
    meta = [r[0] for r in con.execute("SELECT note FROM meta")]
    con.close()

    # --- map: assets ------------------------------------------------------------
    asset_site = {}
    assets = []
    for rowid, aid, desc, site in assets_raw:
        key = norm_key(aid)
        asset_site[key] = site
        assets.append({
            "site": site,
            "source_system": SOURCE_SYSTEM,
            "source_ref": f"{db.name}:assets/{aid}",
            "as_of": None,  # source holds no record timestamp for assets
            "join_status": "matched" if key == aid else "normalized",
            "mismatch_class": None,
            "contradicted_by": None,
            "integrity_flags": None,
            "asset_id": key,
            "asset_id_verbatim": aid,
            "location": None,  # source has no location field
        })

    # --- map: maintenance_work_orders ------------------------------------------
    mwos, unmapped_values = [], []
    for rowid, wo, aid, opened, closed, wo_type, downtime_min, note in wos_raw:
        key = norm_key(aid)
        flags = []
        od, cd = parse_date(opened), parse_date(closed)
        if isinstance(od, dt.date) and isinstance(cd, dt.date) and cd < od:
            flags.append("end_before_start")
        for d in (od, cd):
            if isinstance(d, dt.date) and d > TODAY:
                flags.append("future_timestamp")
        matched = key in asset_site
        mwos.append({
            "site": asset_site.get(key),  # work_orders has no site; inherited via asset
            "source_system": SOURCE_SYSTEM,
            "source_ref": f"{db.name}:work_orders/{wo}",
            "as_of": closed or opened,  # date only, zone not stated by the source
            "join_status": ("matched" if key == aid else "normalized") if matched else "unmatched",
            "mismatch_class": None if matched else 1,
            "contradicted_by": None,
            "integrity_flags": ";".join(sorted(set(flags))) or None,
            "maintenance_wo": wo,
            "asset_id": key,
            "asset_id_verbatim": aid,
            "opened_date": opened,
            "closed_date": closed,
            "close_out_notes": note,
        })
        unmapped_values.append({"maintenance_wo": wo, "wo_type": wo_type,
                                "downtime_min": downtime_min})

    # --- write ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def write_csv(name, cols, rows):
        with open(out / name, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=cols)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(rows)

    write_csv("assets.csv", ASSET_COLS, assets)
    write_csv("maintenance_work_orders.csv", MWO_COLS, mwos)

    hash_after = sha256(db)
    results = {
        "run_at": dt.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "source_file": db.name,
        "source_meta": meta,
        "read_only": {
            "uri_mode": "ro",
            "pragma_query_only": query_only,
            "sha256_before": hash_before,
            "sha256_after": hash_after,
            "file_unchanged": hash_before == hash_after,
        },
        "schema_drift": None,
        "completeness": {
            "assets": {"source_count": n_assets_src, "mapped": len(assets)},
            "work_orders": {"source_count": n_wo_src, "mapped": len(mwos)},
            "open_wos": {"v_open_work_orders": n_open_view,
                         "work_orders_closed_is_null": n_open_tbl,
                         "mapped_open": sum(1 for m in mwos if m["closed_date"] is None)},
        },
        "join": {"unmatched_work_orders": [m["maintenance_wo"] for m in mwos
                                          if m["join_status"] == "unmatched"]},
        "integrity_flags": {m["maintenance_wo"]: m["integrity_flags"]
                            for m in mwos if m["integrity_flags"]},
        "unmapped_fields_held_out": unmapped_values,
    }
    (out / "test-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    print("\n=== assets (mapped) ===")
    for a in assets:
        print(a)
    print("\n=== maintenance_work_orders (mapped) ===")
    for m in mwos:
        print(m)
    if hash_before != hash_after:
        raise SystemExit("SOURCE FILE CHANGED DURING RUN - investigate")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

-- DRAFT for the CMMS database owner to review, create and own. NOT applied:
-- this run had read-only access and created nothing in the source file.
-- Purpose: give the plugin a stable, narrow read surface so a change to the
-- underlying tables breaks loudly at the view (owner edits the view) instead of
-- silently changing what the connector returns.
-- Scope: assets and maintenance work orders only (open AND closed). The existing
-- v_open_work_orders view omits closed work orders, close dates and downtime,
-- which breakdown-diagnosis needs for history, so it is not sufficient alone.

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_plugin_assets AS
SELECT
  asset_id,      -- -> assets.asset_id_verbatim (normalized copy -> assets.asset_id)
  site           -- -> assets.site
  -- description: no column on the dataset's assets tab; held out (see mapping)
  -- location: not held by this CMMS -> assets.location stays null
FROM assets;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_plugin_maintenance_work_orders AS
SELECT
  w.wo           AS maintenance_wo,     -- -> maintenance_work_orders.maintenance_wo
  w.asset_id     AS asset_id,           -- -> asset_id_verbatim (normalized -> asset_id)
  a.site         AS site,               -- -> site (work_orders has no site; via asset)
  w.opened       AS opened_date,        -- -> opened_date (date only, zone unstated)
  w.closed       AS closed_date,        -- -> closed_date (NULL = still open, not unknown)
  w.note         AS note,               -- -> close_out_notes (verbatim; see open question)
  w.wo_type      AS wo_type,            -- no dataset column yet (contract bump needed)
  w.downtime_min AS downtime_min        -- no dataset column yet (contract bump needed)
FROM work_orders w
LEFT JOIN assets a ON a.asset_id = w.asset_id;

-- SQLite has no GRANT. Read-only access is enforced by the consumer opening the
-- file with mode=ro and PRAGMA query_only=ON, and by file-system permissions:
-- the account the connector runs under should have read, not write, on the file.
-- For a server-hosted CMMS database the equivalent is a dedicated integration
-- login granted SELECT on these two views only.

I've connected the plugin to your CMMS file with read-only access and tested it on the real data. It read all 3 assets and all 3 work orders, and every work order joined to an asset. I haven't registered the connection yet: first I need you to confirm nothing you expected is missing.

**How it connects:** the plugin reads the database file directly, and can't write to it. That is the only workable option here:
- **No vendor or community connector was searched for.** The system is fictitious with no product name, and this session has no web search.
- **No API exists**, because the target is just a database file.
- **No login is involved**, since the file has none.

Read-only is enforced twice, by how the file is opened and by a setting on the connection. A fingerprint (hash) of the file was identical before and after the run, so nothing was changed. Each run reads the file as it is at that moment; nothing is scheduled.

## What I read back

**Assets (site EPW1)**
| asset_id | site | location | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| HMC-01 | EPW1 | not in CMMS | Horizontal machining centre (not mapped) |
| VMC-02 | EPW1 | not in CMMS | Vertical machining centre (not mapped) |
| VMC-03 | EPW1 | not in CMMS | Vertical machining centre (not mapped) |

**Maintenance work orders**
| maintenance_wo | asset_id | opened_date | closed_date | close_out_notes | wo_type (not mapped) | downtime_min (not mapped) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MW-152 | VMC-03 | 2026-08-11 | 2026-08-11 | coolant pump replaced | CM | 40 |
| MW-160 | VMC-02 | 2026-09-23 | 2026-09-24 | spindle hot after long cycle; chiller topped up | CM | 95 |
| MW-170 | VMC-02 | 2026-11-10 | *open* | spindle overload / overtemp - open | CM | not recorded |

VMC-02 has had two spindle-temperature work orders in about seven weeks, and one is still open. That history is now readable by `breakdown-diagnosis`.

## Field mapping
The left column is the CMMS field; the right is where it lands in the shared dataset the plugin's other skills read.

| CMMS field | Dataset column | Change made | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| assets.asset_id | `asset_id_verbatim` / `asset_id` | Trimmed and upper-cased | Matches on 3 of 3 |
| assets.site | `site` | None | Matches on 3 of 3 |
| work_orders.wo | `maintenance_wo` | None | Matches on 3 of 3 |
| work_orders.asset_id | `asset_id_verbatim` / `asset_id` | Trimmed and upper-cased | 3 of 3 joined to an asset |
| site, via the asset | `site` | Work orders carry no site, so it's taken from the asset | Matches on 3 of 3 |
| opened | `opened_date` | Date only | Column name is my proposal |
| closed | `closed_date` | Blank means open, not zero | Matches on 3 of 3 |
| closed, or opened if still open | `as_of` | Date only, no time zone | Proposed |
| note | `close_out_notes` | Copied unchanged | Proposed (see question 2) |
| description, wo_type, downtime_min | **Not mapped** | None | The dataset has no column for these yet |

The three unmapped fields are kept aside in the run record, not dropped. Adding `wo_type` (corrective or planned) and downtime minutes would need a change to the dataset's definition. The downtime log needs start and end times per stoppage, which this CMMS doesn't record. Asset location isn't held in the CMMS at all.

- **The file is moved:** the connector fails to open it.
- **Someone points this at a live production CMMS database:** that risks locking it. Point it at a copy, a replica or the views instead.
